AW-STUDY-0028 · Shader experiment

Storybook Light

Can the browser engine paint the soft clay, animated-film look in your picture? Yes. The scene beside it is live: drag to look around, slide the line to compare plain three.js with the full look, and switch each part on or off. The figures are simple stand-ins; the light is the experiment.

The recipe, part by part

Every part is a few lines of shader code. Each one fakes something a film renderer would compute the slow way.

Verdict

  • The light is in reach today. Soft wrap light, warm rim, glowing ears and cheeks, soft contact shadows, the green haze, the round background blur and the gentle glow all run live in the browser engine, with no new tools.
  • Half the look is the models, not the shaders. Your picture gets its charm from sculpted, soft shapes (big noses, chunky fingers, beard clumps, thick grass). The same light on hero-quality models is what would close the gap.
  • It fits a phone. The haze, grade and glow are cheap. Lens blur and soft shadows are the costly parts; they run at half resolution and can drop out on older phones.
  • The whole game can drive it. Sun colour, haze colour and grade are three numbers, so one game signal (time of day, a storm, a mood) can move them all together.
